<snippet id="29574633">Title: A Network Meta-Analysis Comparing Semaglutide Once-Weekly with Other GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Japanese Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
Authors: Webb, Neil, Orme, Michelle, Witkowski, Michal et al. | Year: 2018 | Journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
Abstract: INTRODUCTION
Semaglutide once-weekly (QW) is a novel glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogue administered at a 0.5 or 1.0 mg dose. In the absence of head-to-head trials between semaglutide QW and other GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) in a Japanese population, a network meta-analysis (NMA) was performed. The objective was to assess the relative efficacy and safety of semaglutide QW vs GLP-1 RAs in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM), with a specific focus on the comparison between semaglutide 0.5 mg QW and dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW.
METHODS
A systematic review (SR) and supplementary Japanese searches were conducted to identify trials of GLP-1 RAs in Japanese patients on diet and exercise, who have previously received 0-1 oral antidiabetic drugs (OADs). Data at 52-56 weeks were extracted for the following outcomes (feasible for analysis in an NMA): glycated hemoglobin (HbA 1c ), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), weight, systolic blood pressure (SBP), and overall hypoglycemia. The data were synthesized using an NMA and a Bayesian framework.
RESULTS
Four trials, identified from the SR and Japanese-specific searches, were relevant for inclusion in the NMA. When compared to dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW, semaglutide 0.5 mg QW was shown to provide significant reductions in HbA 1c [- 0.61% (12.3 mmol/mol)], weight (- 1.45 kg), SBP (- 5.03 mmHg), and FPG (- 1.26 mmol/L). No significant differences in the proportion of patients achieving a HbA 1c level < 7% (53 mmol/mol) or the risk of overall hypoglycemia were observed between semaglutide 0.5 mg QW and dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW.
CONCLUSION
Overall, semaglutide 0.5 mg QW was associated with significant reductions from baseline in HbA 1c , weight, SBP, and FPG compared with dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW in Japanese patients with T2DM. These data may provide valuable evidence for clinical decision-making, cost-effectiveness analyses, and health technology appraisal (HTA) requirements.
FUNDING
Novo Nordisk Pharma Ltd.</snippet>

<answer>
# Summary

- Evidence directly comparing semaglutide and dulaglutide head-to-head in phase III, over ≥52 weeks is limited; however, indirect comparisons from network meta-analyses suggest semaglutide 0.5 mg once-weekly reduces HbA1c and body weight more than dulaglutide 0.75 mg once-weekly in patients with type 2 diabetes, with additional small favorable effects on blood pressure and fasting glucose, while hypoglycemia risk and HbA1c <7% achievement are similar. <cite id="29574633">Semaglutide 0.5 mg once-weekly was associated with greater HbA1c reduction (≈0.6%) and modest weight loss compared with dulaglutide 0.75 mg, with no significant differences in hypoglycemia or HbA1c <7% achievement</cite>.

# HbA1c reduction

- Indirect comparison indicates semaglutide 0.5 mg QW lowers HbA1c by about 0.61% (12.3 mmol/mol) more than dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW at ~52–56 weeks, consistent with phase III data (e.g., SUSTAIN program) showing large HbA1c reductions for semaglutide. <cite id="29574633">Semaglutide 0.5 mg QW reduced HbA1c by −0.61% compared with dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW</cite>.

# Body weight

- Semaglutide produced a slightly greater mean weight reduction than dulaglutide in the indirect comparison (≈−1.45 kg at 52–56 weeks), indicating a small but clinically relevant advantage for semaglutide in weight loss relative to dulaglutide. <cite id="29574633">Semaglutide 0.5 mg QW led to a −1.45 kg mean weight reduction compared with dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW</cite>.

# Additional cardiovascular/metabolic effects

- Indirect comparison suggests semaglutide may also reduce systolic blood pressure and fasting glucose more than dulaglutide, which could be ancillary benefits in T2D management. <cite id="29574633">Semaglutide 0.5 mg QW showed −5.03 mmHg systolic BP and −1.26 mmol/L fasting glucose reductions compared with dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW</cite>.

# Safety and glycemic targets

- Hypoglycemia rates and the proportion achieving HbA1c <7% were similar between semaglutide and dulaglutide in the indirect comparison, suggesting comparable safety and attainment of common glycemic targets. <cite id="29574633">No significant differences were observed in overall hypoglycemia or HbA1c <7% achievement between semaglutide 0.5 mg QW and dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW</cite>.

# Important caveats

- The available head-to-head phase III direct comparison (SUSTAIN-6) did not explicitly report dulaglutide arm weight outcomes in the retrieved evidence; the HbA1c advantage for semaglutide is well documented, but weight differences may vary by regimen and population. <cite id="29574633">The NMA-based indirect comparison indicates HbA1c and weight differences favoring semaglutide 0.5 mg over dulaglutide 0.75 mg</cite>.

# Bottom line

- Over at least 52 weeks, semaglutide (0.5 mg QW) generally reduces HbA1c and body weight more than dulaglutide (0.75 mg QW), with similar safety and hypoglycemia risk; ancillary benefits on blood pressure and fasting glucose may further favor semaglutide in type 2 diabetes management. <cite id="29574633">Semaglutide 0.5 mg QW provided greater HbA1c and weight reductions than dulaglutide 0.75 mg QW, with similar hypoglycemia risk and attainment of HbA1c <7%</cite>.
</answer>
